entrypoints.summary: A project Developer runs an unprotected-branch pipeline on a self-hosted Docker runner and writes attacker-selected content under /cache.
A protected-branch pipeline subsequently runs on the same runner slot and mounts /cache.

affected_components.role: Pre-fix registration logic automatically adds /cache when Docker cache disabling is false.

affected_components.file: GitInfo structure and GitLab Runner Docker executor cache-volume handling
affected_components.role: The two remediation MRs respectively add protected status sent to Runner and separate cache volumes by protected state.

code_slices.fixed: Server MR describes adding protected status to GitInfo sent to Runner; Runner MR describes using separate local cache volumes for protected and unprotected builds.
code_slices.surrounding_context: Fetched merge-request excerpts do not provide the patch diff or test source.
code_slices.vulnerable: askDocker() checks existing Docker volumes and appends /cache unless DisableCache is set.

negative_controls: Use distinct protected and unprotected cache volumes; the runner MR describes validating that two volumes are used.
observability.positive_marker: The protected job can list and read /cache/openme.txt written in the unprotected job.

preconditions: A self-hosted Docker runner handles both unprotected and protected branch jobs for the project.
Docker cache is enabled at registration, causing /cache to be added.
The attacker has Developer access sufficient to run an unprotected-branch pipeline.
A protected-branch job later runs on the same runner slot.

sources.concept: unprotected pipeline write to a runner-local cache

impact.affected_asset: Integrity of protected-branch pipeline execution and confidentiality of artifacts or secrets available to protected jobs.
impact.attacker_capability: A Developer able to run an unprotected-branch pipeline can persist attacker-selected files in the shared cache for a protected-branch job on the same self-hosted Docker runner.
impact.security_effect: Cross-trust-domain disclosure of cache contents is directly demonstrated; arbitrary code execution in a protected pipeline or secret exfiltration is reported as the potential consequence of poisoned cache consumption.

causal_trace.summary: Docker-runner registration invokes askDocker(), which appends /cache to Docker volumes when DisableCache is false, including where the project CI configuration does not define a cache.
The resulting named cache volume is scoped to the runner slot rather than branch protection state or cache key, allowing protected and unprotected pipeline jobs to use one mutable physical directory.
An unprotected-branch job writes content to /cache; a later protected-branch job on the same runner slot mounts that same directory and can list and read the attacker-written file.

The disclosure states that cache poisoning can cause a subsequent protected-branch job to execute attacker-controlled code or expose protected-pipeline secrets; the supplied reproducer directly demonstrates file persistence and read access, not a payload-execution run.

failure.operation: Reuse of a runner-slot-scoped Docker /cache volume across unprotected and protected pipeline jobs

primary_invariant.kind: trust-domain isolation for persistent build state
primary_invariant.statement: A protected pipeline must not mount or consume mutable local cache state written by an unprotected pipeline.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The Docker cache volume is keyed to a shared runner slot and is automatically mounted at /cache without a protected/unprotected trust-state partition.

quality.review_notes: The public disclosure supplies registration, attacker and victim pipeline programs, and an observable protected-job read of attacker-created cache content. It does not supply an observed payload-execution run, so protected-job code execution and secret exfiltration remain report-stated consequences. Merge-request pages establish remediation intent and linkage, but their fetched excerpts do not include diffs or tests; detailed implementation semantics are not asserted.

remediation.invariant_restored: Protected and unprotected builds use distinct local cache volumes after the runner receives the build's protected status.
mitigation_classes: propagate protected-branch status from GitLab to Runner
partition persistent Docker cache volumes by protected versus unprotected build state

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker has Developer access and can execute a pipeline on an unprotected branch assigned to the shared self-hosted Docker runner.
data_structure_invariants: Cache-volume identity must include the protected/unprotected execution trust state when the volume persists across jobs.
A protected job must not receive a mutable cache directory written by unprotected jobs.
state_context.state_machine: Runner registration configures a persistent /cache mount; an unprotected job writes that state; a later protected job on the same runner slot mounts and reads it.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: GitLab Runner 18.0.2 (revision 4d7093e1), as reported in the disclosure

target.component: Docker executor registration and local /cache volume selection

oracle.expected_negative: With protected/unprotected cache-volume separation, same-project protected and unprotected builds should use different local volumes, so the protected job should not observe state created in the unprotected volume.
oracle.expected_positive: Before mitigation, after an unprotected job creates /cache/openme.txt, a protected job on the same runner slot can list and read that file.
